answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by anchoring each identity to sequential, non-parallelizable work: like layers of shale, reputation must accumulate in order, one epoch at a time, not in parallel across many accounts. A new identity starts in a shallow lagoon of low trust, with tiny limits, and only earns deeper access after verified, time-spaced contributions. An attacker making a thousand fakes must therefore pay a thousand times the wall-clock time, not just cheap parallel compute, so mass fakery becomes slow and uneconomical.
